column2: The song retains established heart, exalted horn, widened mouth against enemies and joy in Thy salvation, with the shift into direct divine address.
column3: I rejoice gives the present consequence of the Greek aorist euphranthen; I rejoiced or I have rejoiced remain closer tense alternatives for literary review.

column2: The three holiness/righteousness comparisons retain our God and direct Thee; authored lineation gives each selected parallel clause its own line.
The three prohibitions on boasting, lofty speech and grandiose words lead to the Lord's knowledge and preparation of His undertakings; lineation distinguishes the four clauses.
column3: His undertakings preserves the selected possessive and divine subject, rather than importing a weighing of human deeds.

column2: The mighty bow's weakness contrasts with the weak girding themselves with strength; a line break exposes the two halves without changing wording.
The full are diminished, the hungry leave the land, the barren bears seven and the many-child mother weakens; four authored lines retain each reversal.
column3: Left the land is the selected reading and is not replaced with ceased to hunger or found employment.

column2: The Lord's killing/life-giving and descent-to-Hades/ascent pairs remain as two balanced lines with divine agency intact.
Poverty/wealth and humiliation/exaltation remain paired divine actions; the existing two-line display is retained.
Earth and dung heap give way to rulers of peoples and an inherited glorious throne; authored lines distinguish raising, lifting, seating and granting.
column3: Needy and poor distinguish penes/ptochos here without claiming an exhaustive socioeconomic definition of either term.

column2: Granting a prayer, blessing the righteous one's years and strength's insufficiency remain; lineation preserves the participle, past blessing and final general statement.
column3: Prayer for euche in the giving-to-one-who-prays wordplay is provisional alongside the possible vow/request sense; no familiar guarding-feet clause replaces it.

column2: The full expanded wisdom passage remains between the weakened opponent/holy Lord and heavenly ascent, thunder, judgment, strength to our kings and His anointed's horn; authored lines expose all clause parallels.
column3: Our kings remains plural and present gives contrasts with future will judge/raise. No apparatus collation or NT quotation harmonization is claimed for this expanded selected passage.

column2: They leave the child before the Lord and return to Armathaim; the child ministers before both the Lord and Eli in their distinct relationships.
Eli's sons are called pestilent and do not know the Lord, preserving the selected descriptor without a substituted sons-of-Belial phrase.
Remove claimed before right: the Greek states the priest's dikaioma without a separate qualifier questioning the claim; the boiling meat and three-pronged hook remain.
column3: The narrative condemns the conduct in verse 17. Removing claimed does not endorse it; right is the inherited lexical choice, with custom/practice alternatives still requiring review.

column2: The hook enters one of three vessels and the priest takes whatever it brings up; this practice applies to all Israel's worshipers at Shiloh.
Before the fat is burned, the servant demands roasting meat and emphatically refuses boiled meat from the cauldron; the first-person refusal remains.
The worshiper asks for proper prior fat-burning and then permits taking what the soul desires; the servant instead demands immediate giving and threatens force.
column3: He in the reply is the servant inferred from dialogue, not newly named in the Greek clause.

column2: The servants' sin is very great before the Lord because they reject His sacrifice; the selected causal evaluation remains explicit.
Samuel ministers as a child girded with ephoud bar; the transliterated garment expression is not silently replaced by linen ephod.
His mother makes a little double cloak and brings it annually with the yearly sacrifice; both recurring-days expressions retain their contextual annual sense.
column3: Double cloak for diplois is provisional garment terminology; its exact construction is not independently established here.

column2: Eli blesses Elkanah and his wife with offspring from this woman in return for the loan, and the man departs; the loan vocabulary links 1:28.
The Lord visits Hannah, who bears three additional sons and two daughters; Samuel grows before the Lord in a separate closing clause.
Very old Eli hears his sons' conduct toward Israel; no additional sexual-misconduct clause is imported from a longer textual form.
He challenges their actions by the report from all the Lord's people, retaining the mouth image and the public scope.
The negative report is stated twice, with two prohibitions and the consequence that the people do not serve God.
column3: So that renders the final negative infinitive as a consequence; its exact explanatory relation remains syntactically open.

column2: Human-against-human sin permits prayer by unnamed others, but sin against the Lord prompts who-will-pray; their refusal to listen is linked to the Lord's emphatic intention to destroy.
column3: People supplies the unexpressed plural praying subject, without identifying a priestly mediator. Divine agency is not weakened to mere permission.

column2: Samuel's continuing growth and goodness with both the Lord and people remain, expressed idiomatically as in favour.
column3: In favour is the inherited contextual interpretation of agathon with meta; good in relation to both is a closer alternative.

column2: A man of God reports the Lord's emphatic self-revelation to Eli's paternal house while they were slaves to Pharaoh's house in Egypt.
Selection from Israel's tribes leads to priestly service, altar ascent, incense and bearing ephoud; all the Israelites' fire offerings are given for food.
column3: Tribes renders sceptres metonymically in the selection formula; the image and cultic terms remain recorded without a completed specialist study.

column2: The shameless eye, preference for sons over God and firstfruits of every sacrifice remain the accusation's elements.
column3: They bless themselves gives the sons as contextual subject of the infinitive; Eli or a broader group may be implicated, and the exact reflexive/passive force remains open.

column2: The earlier perpetual-house statement is recalled and rejected, followed by honour for honourers and dishonour for the despiser.
column3: Only is supported here by the selected restrictive alla e construction; it is retained as a contextual decision, not removed by a general word-replacement rule.

column2: Behold introduces coming days of destruction for Eli's offspring and his paternal house's offspring; the repeated seed/offspring objects remain.
No old man of his will be in My house all the days; the selected divine-house location is not changed to his own house.

Propose I will spare a man of yours at My altar instead of I will not destroy every man of yours from My altar. Spare renders the negative destruction clause affirmatively, keeping its indefinite singular and making the exception intelligible in English; the close draft retains the negative form.
column3: At My altar interprets not being destroyed from the altar as remaining in its service; the following his eyes/his soul supports an unspecified surviving man. His identity, the indefinite’s exact scope and the purpose/result force of the infinitives remain open. No exact count of all survivors is supplied.

column2: Hophni and Phinehas are named as the sign's two sons, both dying in one day; the shared day is explicit.
The Lord raises a faithful priest to do everything in His heart and soul, builds a faithful house and promises continuing service before His anointed; faithful repeats deliberately.
The remaining household member bows for a silver obol and asks a priestly office for bread; the small coin and dependent livelihood remain without modern monetary conversion.
